They're unaware that they may be met at the US border by armed soldiers who will fire at them if necessary to bar them from the land of opportunity. Apparently the Latin American leftists aren't telling them that because he doesn't serve their purpose. And the American regime certainly isn't sending emissaries to tell them that either because they are so useful the migrants for scaring voters in the upcoming election. The migrants know nothing about any upcoming US election. Despite some efforts of Mexico to stop or slow the caravan, it continues. Now, leaderless, organic. Any master plans by organizers fallen by the roadside, just the people themselves. They move as if one body, the way starlings swoop and wheel and circle in great dipping and rising whorls and sheets across the sky, in what's called a murmuration. But each dot in this quantilist image is a human being. In some towns they pass through, volunteer nurses treat people for blisters, for sunburn, for dehydration, for broken bones. They treat diabetics who have no medicine. So far two women have given birth along the way, and one birth was still born. The women. Oh my God, the women. They are harassed and assaulted. They try to help each other. The men yell at them to keep up, but the men carry only parcels, and the women carry parcels and children. Anyone who has ever been around a two-year-old child for one hour knows that the demands of that toddler are ferocious. Imagine, then, trudging in flip-flops on rocky roads and hot pavement and muddy fields eight to ten miles a day hour after day after week with a two-year-old strapped to your back or riding your hip or a two-year-old and a three-year-old or two and four and seven-year-olds hanging onto your skirt. All the little ones whining, hungry, thirsty, sleepy, scared, oh scared, wailing for attention. Decent people in towns and cities and rural areas along the way bring out pots of food, mostly rice and beans. But sometimes there are days with no food except for the little they might have saved from what they brought with them. One night in a small town a local band started playing and a few young migrants danced because it's hard to stamp out the human hunger for a moment of happiness. In a corner of the square, a group of older women knelt, saying their rosary together, because it's hard to erase superstition, and even harder to erase hope. These are Donald Trump's calloused criminals and terrorists, swept north by cynical politics of men on the right and on the left. They're just looking for work and food and a little respite. They want to stop. They're desperate to rest. Freedom, freedom is abstract, but they know they want some peace. So thirsty, so tired. They want the baby to stop crying. Oh God, let the baby stop. Let the baby stop crying. Let it stop. This is biblical, yes. This is medieval too. This is happening now. This is a crime against humanity. Those are my fighting words. Add yours on Twitter and remember to tag us at WMC Live and use the hashtag fighting words. And that's our show for today. You can follow me on Twitter at TheRobinMorgan and on Facebook at facebook.com slash TheRobinMorgan. Check out my blog at robinmorgan.net and find my latest book, Dark Matter, Wherever Books Are Sold. Opinions expressed on this program do not necessarily represent the Women's Media Center. Here's the family for our show. Executive producer as well as founding and sustaining sponsor Regina K. Scully, WMC president and co-executive producer of this program, Julie Burton. I'm Robin Morgan, your producer and host. Thank you for being with us. Join us again next time on Women's Media Center Live.

The U.S. supported Honduran President Juan Hernandez despite evidence of corruption and excessive power.
More than 200–300 Hondurans leave daily due to violence and poverty.
The leftist opposition in Honduras initiated the caravan as a response to government failure.

False narratives spread widely including claims of migrant payments by George Soros and fabricated videos.

assumptions.text: Political leaders on both the right and left manipulate vulnerable populations for strategic gain.
The suffering of migrants is exploited by powerful actors to advance electoral and ideological agendas.
Media narratives are shaped by political interests rather than objective truth.
Fearmongering effectively mobilizes specific voter demographics in U.S. elections.
Migrants lack awareness of how their movement is being politicized.
Humanitarian needs like food, shelter, and medical care are insufficiently addressed during displacement.
Collective action among marginalized people reflects shared desperation rather than coordinated strategy.
Cultural and religious practices provide psychological resilience amid extreme hardship.
Violence and exploitation against women and children are systemic outcomes of forced migration.
The U.S. government prioritizes political messaging over humanitarian responsibility.
